plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin DE + hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 6 lesional-AD vs 6 control skin samples, raw Salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), single batch, unpaired. One sample (sample_01) has a library size ~4x below median — per the sourced rule (R-0008), this is kept through QC and reported, not silently dropped, since DESeq2 size factors already account for depth. Track 1 runs sample structure QC (library sizes, VST-based PCA, sample-distance heatmap) so the low-depth sample can be visually assessed before any modeling decision, then a minimal count pre-filter, PyDESeq2 normalization (median-of-ratios) and Wald test with an explicit reference level (Control) and named contrast, apeglm-style LFC shrinkage, and BH-adjusted results with independent filtering (all in Python via pydeseq2, respecting the user's Python-only constraint). Track 2 takes the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic, per the disputed-metric rule R-0108 — chosen because it is the DESeq2-native, uncertainty-scaled statistic) into gseapy prerank against the locally staged MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets, with Reactome as a same-organism follow-up collection, both present in the reference store. A final report step consolidates DE and enrichment results with the required reproducibility record (versions, seed, thresholds, collection versions) and states the low-depth-sample caveat and the enrichment method-dependence caveat explicitly.
